subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 47-year-old man in a resource-limited region presents with 4 weeks of watery diarrhea and a painful, hyperpigmented, scaly rash over his neck and the backs of his hands that appears only in sun-exposed skin. His diet consists almost entirely of untreated corn. His family notes that he has become forgetful and has begun to have visual hallucinations. Examination shows a broad collar-shaped band of dermatitis around the base of the neck.
question: Deficiency of which of the following vitamins best explains this presentation?
explanation_correct: This patient has pellagra, the classic niacin deficiency syndrome with the 3 Ds: diarrhea, dementia (including hallucinations), and dermatitis that is photo-distributed and classically forms a broad collar around the neck (Casal necklace). Untreated corn is a poor source of bioavailable niacin and tryptophan, so corn-based diets predispose to deficiency. Niacin is the precursor of NAD+ and NADP+, which are essential cofactors for dehydrogenases in redox reactions.

explanation_incorrect.A: Thiamine deficiency causes Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome and beriberi, with confabulation, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, or heart failure rather than a photo-distributed rash and diarrhea.
explanation_incorrect.B: Riboflavin deficiency causes cheilosis, a magenta tongue, and corneal vascularization but not the dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia triad.
explanation_incorrect.D: Pyridoxine deficiency causes peripheral neuropathy, seizures, and sideroblastic anemia and does not produce the Casal necklace rash.
explanation_incorrect.E: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes macrocytic anemia and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord; diarrhea and photo-distributed dermatitis are not typical.

educationalObjective: Niacin deficiency causes pellagra with the 3 Ds (diarrhea, dementia, dermatitis), and corn-based diets are a classic risk factor.
